display.title: Rabbi Akiva's Great Rule: Love Your Fellow as Yourself
display.summary_short: Rabbi Akiva taught that loving your fellow Jew is a great rule of the Torah; the Alter Rebbe adds that Ahavas Yisroel leads to love of Hashem.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. It opens with the closing lesson of a story about Rabbi Akiva: how much he loved Hashem, ready to give his life to learn Torah and keep mitzvos, and how Hashem blesses those who keep the mitzvos with firm faith. Uncle Yossi then turns to Rabbi Akiva's most famous saying from the Gemara: the Torah's command to love your fellow as yourself is not just another rule but a great, all-embracing one. Through Ahavas Yisroel we come to love Hashem and keep all the other mitzvos, as the Alter Rebbe taught. He explains with a simple example: if you truly love a friend, you also show love to the friends he loves. Hashem loves every single Jew, so to show our love for Hashem we must openly love everyone He loves.
display.lesson: Love every Jew, because Hashem loves each one; Ahavas Yisroel leads to Ahavas Hashem.

date.note: Cut from episode 122 (Sefirah 5744); re-aired in many later episodes.
